sources.title: Michel Abitbol, Les Arma de Tombouctou (1977)
sources.note: Original historical research. Pages 445 and 446 directly read, the latter with ?pageId=T1_446. Origins, river garrisons and military divisions becoming family groups.

sources.title: Mauro Nobili, Sultan, Caliph, and the Renewer of the Faith: introduction
sources.note: Cambridge original scholarship, indexed excerpt page 8: Moroccan withdrawal, local garrisons and de facto independence by 1660. Direct PDF fetch failed; indexed text checked.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Ancient Manuscripts from the Desert Libraries of Timbuktu
sources.note: Museum descriptions of objects 1, 2, 4, 11 and 16 directly read. The 1733 copy is dated; other manuscript examples are explicitly contextual and not assigned invented copy dates.

sources.title: Al-Sadi, Tarikh al-Sudan, Arabic edition by Houdas (1898)
sources.note: Digitization of University of Toronto copy, Arabic printed page 2, heading before first chapter: الباب الاول. OCR text directly read. Original text is seventeenth century; this witness is the 1898 edition, not an autograph. Catalogue confirms Arabic, Paris E. Leroux, 1898. No visual verification claimed.

sources.title: Ariela Marcus-Sells, Sorcery or Science? (2022), chapter 1
sources.note: Original Penn State University Press scholarship in readable book reproduction. Printed pages 36 to 38 describe assimilation, local scholars, 1737 defeat, 1755 recovery, 1770 pressure and 1787 capture.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Timbuktu
sources.note: Directly read Statement of Outstanding Universal Value, authenticity and management: three mosques, earthen construction, maintenance and community involvement.

sources.title: MINUSMA, Exchanges on traditional and formal justice in Timbuktu (14 February 2023)
sources.note: Full indexed official report checked after direct fetch failed. Mouhoumoudou Touré, Arma community chief of Gao, discusses small family/land disputes and referral to state justice.

sources.title: Stephen Behrendt, A. J. H. Latham and David Northrup, The Diary of Antera Duke (2010)
sources.note: Oxford University Press edition, original diary transcription and historical research. Publisher preview directly read, printed pages 2 to 3, 9 and 16. Writing sample is the initial phrase before first dated entry of 18 January 1785; transcription survives the lost original.

sources.title: Stephen Behrendt and Eric Graham, African Merchants, Notables and the Slave Trade at Old Calabar, 1720
sources.note: Original archival research, History in Africa 30 (2003). Extract and notes directly read: Hannover supplies and enslaved people, note 46 anchorage fees in 1785.

sources.title: A. W. Wilkie and J. K. Macgregor, Industrial Training in Africa: Calabar mission (1914), page 745
sources.note: Contemporary missionary account in International Review of Missions 3, pages 742 to 747. Indexed original page 745 read; direct fetch failed. Institutional perspective explicitly identified, not independent evaluation of education quality.

sources.title: Southern Nigeria annual report for 1906, published 1908
sources.note: Directly read primary colonial report, printed page 50, paragraphs 111 to 113. Hospitals segregated in reporting. St Margaret’s 798 cases and 7,129 outpatients are administrative counts, not a census of all illness.

sources.title: British Museum, covered gourd bowl Af1911,1215.6.a-b
sources.note: Museum catalogue directly indexed: Calabar, 1911 or earlier, probably Ibibio manufacture. Curator rejects the old register’s identification of decoration as Nsibidi. Do not treat Calabar collection location as Efik maker identification.

sources.title: International Court of Justice, Cameroon v. Nigeria, judgment of 10 October 2002
sources.note: Official majority judgment, paragraphs 203 to 208. English indexed paragraph 203 and French official judgment paragraphs 207 to 208 checked. Treaty and indirect administration; paragraph 208 records Nigeria’s answer that it could not supply a precise endpoint, rather than a judicial determination of impossibility.

sources.title: University of Calabar, institutional history
sources.note: Institution’s postgraduate-school history directly indexed: 1975 establishment, 1976 teaching in three faculties and 977 initial students. Used for dated later city continuity, not nineteenth-century state identity.

sources.title: Niger cultural heritage ministry, Old Zinder, Birni and the sultanate (2006)
sources.note: State-party submission hosted by UNESCO, not an inscribed World Heritage property. Direct indexed text read. Coordinates, approximate 1736 origins, 1812 seat, walls and surviving customary palace.

sources.title: F. W. Sowers and Manzo Issoufou, Precolonial Agroforestry: the Sultanate of Damagaram (1992)
sources.note: Original field research and historical study in ICRAF/ICRISAT proceedings, printed pages 171 to 175. Directly read, especially historical context, protected species, seed distribution and 1899 colonial transformation.

sources.title: Anne-Monique Bardagot and Ali Bida, Conservation of the palace of the Sultanate of Zinder
sources.note: Original conservation case study, ICCROM Traditional Conservation Practices in Africa, chapter 6, printed pages 42 to 48. Official indexed passages checked; full same-volume reproduction at https://www.scribd.com/document/413288053/ICCROM-ICS02-TraditionalPractices-En directly read. Direct official PDF fetch failed.

sources.title: Dorugu, Life and Travels, dictated account in Schön’s Grammar of the Hausa Language (1862)
sources.note: Primary Hausa narrative and contemporary English translation, printed pages 215 to 217 and 234, directly read. Sample Muka zakka ga Zinder at page 234. Roman-letter transcription by Schön, not an Ajami manuscript or claim Dorugu personally penned it.

sources.title: Seyni Moumouni, Histoire de Zinder: Les manuscrits anciens du Damagaram au Niger (2022)
sources.note: Publisher description of historian/philologist’s edition of an Arabic local chronicle directly read. Only publication, language and chronological scope asserted; manuscript text itself was not accessible.

sources.title: Freedom Narratives, Dorugu Kwage Adamu, FN000058
sources.note: Research database by Mohammed Bashir Salau, primary-source-linked biography: birth southwest of Zinder, enslavement, autobiography. Used to establish regional identity of the quoted narrator, not for unverified manuscript spelling.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Timbuktu vicinity fits a late Arma slice. Periods deliberately extend beyond snapshots; no invented fall in 1783. Manuscript examples belong to the multicultural city and libraries, not exclusively Arma ethnicity. Original writing witness is later printed edition, transparently labeled.

Outline includes Old Calabar/Cross River. Do not conflate with New Calabar/Kalabari further west. Earlier diary evidence explicitly labeled. Colonial endpoint qualified following ICJ discussion. Gourd object likely Ibibio, collected locally, not identified as Efik invention or readable Nsibidi.

Major geometry warning public: Zinder at about 9 E,13.8 N lies southwest of polygon. Chronology predates snapshots and sovereignty ended 1899. Dorugu’s regional childhood is earlier contextual evidence. Heritage submission is tentative, not World Heritage inscription. No exact palace-building year asserted because sources vary in relation to reign chronology.
